title: To, in, from, with: case endings
description: Mark who receives an action and where things happen, with the endings -ke and -e / -te and the postpositions theke, diye, shonge, jonno.

guide.title: -ke: the person on the receiving end
guide.text:
The ending -কে (-ke) marks the person an action is directed at. It covers both the English direct object ('I know Raj') and 'to' ('give it to Raj').

আমি রাজকে চিনি - I know Raj.
রাজকে বলুন - Tell Raj.

It is used for people and animals, and for things only when they are specific and you want to single them out. Ordinary things as objects take no ending at all: আমি ভাত খাই, 'I eat rice'; আমি বইটা পড়েছি, 'I have read the book'.

When a sentence has both a person and a thing, the person gets -কে and comes first: আমাকে একটা কলম দিন, 'me-to a pen give'.

The pronoun forms: আমাকে, আপনাকে, তোমাকে, তোকে, তাকে, ওকে, তাঁকে, ওঁকে; plural আমাদের, আপনাদের, তোমাদের, তাদের, ওদের (the plural object forms are the same as the possessive).

guide.title: -e, -te, -y: in, at, on, to
guide.text:
One ending does the work of 'in', 'at', 'on' and, with verbs of movement, 'to'. Its shape depends on the last sound of the word.

After a consonant: -এ (-e). ঘর - ঘরে (ghore) in the room; বাজার - বাজারে (baajaare) at/to the market; টেবিল - টেবিলে (tebile) on the table.

After আ (aa): -য় (-y). কলকাতা - কলকাতায় (kolkaataay); ঢাকা - ঢাকায় (dhaakaay); রাস্তা - রাস্তায় (raastaay) on the road. (-তে is also heard: ঢাকাতে.)

After any other vowel: -তে (-te). বাড়ি - বাড়িতে (baarite) at home; দিল্লি - দিল্লিতে (dillite) in Delhi.

With a verb of going, the ending is often left off a destination: আমি বাড়ি যাচ্ছি, 'I am going home'; আমি কলকাতা যাব, 'I will go to Kolkata'.

The same ending also means 'by' a means of transport: বাসে (baase) by bus, ট্রেনে (trene) by train, ট্যাক্সিতে (tyaaksite) by taxi.

examples.english: I am going to the market.

guide.title: Postpositions: from, with, for
guide.text:
Other relationships are shown by separate words placed after the noun.

থেকে (theke) 'from, since' follows the plain noun: দিল্লি থেকে, 'from Delhi'; কাল থেকে, 'since yesterday'.

দিয়ে (diye) 'with (a tool), by way of' also follows the plain noun: হাত দিয়ে, 'with the hand'; ছুরি দিয়ে, 'with a knife'; এই রাস্তা দিয়ে, 'along this road'.

সঙ্গে (shonge) 'with, together with' needs the possessive -r on the word before it: বন্ধুর সঙ্গে, 'with a friend'; আমার সঙ্গে, 'with me'. Bangladesh usage prefers সাথে (shaathe).

জন্য (jonno) 'for' also needs the possessive: আপনার জন্য, 'for you'; বাবার জন্য, 'for father'. (জন্যে is a common spoken variant.)

কাছে (kaachhe) 'near; to or at a person' takes the possessive too: স্টেশনের কাছে, 'near the station'; ডাক্তারের কাছে, 'to the doctor'.

examples.english: I am going with a friend.
The shop is near the station.

guide.title: Place words: on, under, inside, in front
guide.text:
Words for position follow the noun in its possessive form, as if you were saying 'at the table's top'.

উপরে (upore) on, above - in Kolkata speech usually ওপরে (opore)
নিচে (niche) under, below
ভেতরে (bhetore) inside - written form ভিতরে
বাইরে (baaire) outside
সামনে (shaamne) in front of
পেছনে (pechhone) behind - written form পিছনে
পাশে (paashe) beside
মধ্যে (moddhe) in the middle of, among, within

So: টেবিলের উপরে, 'on the table'; খাটের নিচে, 'under the bed'; বাড়ির সামনে, 'in front of the house'; দোকানের পাশে, 'next to the shop'.

examples.english: The book is on top of the table.
The cat is under the bed.

phrases.note: The person takes -ke; the thing takes no ending.

phrases.english: I am going to the market.

phrases.note: -te after a vowel other than aa.
Rice meals are traditionally eaten with the right hand.

phrases.english: I cut fruit with a knife.
I am going with a friend.
The book is on top of the table.
The shop is near the station.
The cat is under the bed.
phrases.note: The written form of 'cat' is বিড়াল (biraal).
